title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: Your makerspace assistant has a 900-token system prompt and 500 tokens of tool descriptions. A student types a 30-token question. The model asks for one tool, and the 700-token result comes back. The model's request was 50 tokens. How many input tokens does the second model call use?

options.text: 700 tokens, since only the new tool result is added
730 tokens, since the question and result are new
2,180 tokens, since everything is sent again together
1,430 tokens, since the model's own request is skipped

items.stem: A student chats with your assistant on Monday, then comes back on Thursday in a brand-new session. In one sentence, what must your program do on Monday for the assistant to know anything about the student on Thursday?

Your team can put the 3D-printer manual (8,000 tokens) in the prompt every call, or retrieve 3 pieces of about 300 tokens each. Questions come in all day and the budget is small. Which design is cheaper per request, and why?

options.text: Retrieval, because only about 900 tokens are sent instead of 8,000
Full prompt, because the model then needs no search step at all
Retrieval, because pieces never count toward the window limit
Full prompt, because a larger window makes extra tokens free

items.stem: A call has 2,000 tokens of rules and tools, a 40-token question, and a 3,000-token manual chapter returned by a tool. The model has already used the chapter. Your program replaces it with a 20-token stub before the next call, which adds no other tokens. How many input tokens does that next call use?

Your notes file says a student's laser training is not done, dated three weeks ago, and the student asks to book the laser cutter. In one sentence, what should the assistant do before booking, and why?
